second.QA1_evidence: Sections 2.1 to 2.4 give Eq. (1) instance class (10 random instances, coefficients +1/-1 on the heavy-hex graph), the Figure 2 circuit, angle grids (60 x 120 for p=1; 5 x 11^3 for p=2), DDD pass and scheduling, transpiler level, QA schedule grid (324 combinations) and SA package with default settings.
second.QA2_evidence: Hardware runs on ibm_washington and D-Wave Advantage 4.1/6.1 (Table 1); "all 127 qubits"; "CNOT depth of 6 per round", p=1 and 2; "Each circuit execution used 10,000 samples" (Section 2.2); 500 anneals per D-Wave job (Section 2.3).
second.QA3_evidence: Section 2.4: simulated annealing (dwave-neal) on the same 10 Ising instances after order reduction, default settings, 1000 samples each. Not budget-tuned; Section 4 defers state-of-the-art classical benchmarking to future work.
second.QA4_evidence: Section 2.1: "10 random instances of this class of problems are generated"; synthetic hardware-native Ising models, reproducible from Eq. (1) and stated to be in the public repository. Metric is sample energy distributions (Figures 5 and 6).
second.QA5_evidence: Section 1: "Code, data, and additional figures are available in a public Github repository" (footnote 1, github.com/lanl/QAOA_vs_QA). Link check with curl -I was blocked by the session proxy (403 policy denial), so resolution was not verified.
second.execution: quantum hardware (gate-model QAOA on IBMQ ibm_washington; quantum annealing on D-Wave Advantage_system4.1 and Advantage_system6.1), with a classical simulated annealing comparison
second.scale: QAOA: 127 qubits, p = 1 and 2 rounds, CNOT depth 6 per round, 10,000 shots per circuit, 7200 (p=1) and 6655 (p=2) grid circuits per instance; total transpiled depth not stated. QA: 127 problem variables plus 2 auxiliary qubits per cubic term on Pegasus P16 chips (5627 and 5616 qubits available), 500 anneals per job, annealing times 10 to 2000 microseconds; total physical qubits used per embedding not stated.
second.classical_baseline: Simulated annealing (dwave-neal, default settings, 1000 samples per instance) on the order-reduced Ising models, plus 10,000 uniform random samples; SA performs marginally better than QA (Section 3).
